- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment is positive (≥0.6) and model forecasts are trending up, check for overconfidence; if price drops in next 3–5 days, adjust forecast downward by 1–2%.
- When sentiment is neutral or negative, model often underestimates downside risk; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for downward correction.
- Model tends to overreact to recent volatility; if 3-day moving average of sentiment is rising, reduce forecast slope to avoid overcorrection.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if recent 10-day average is >10% above 30-day mean, apply downward correction of 1–2% per 5-day lag.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to forecast flat or slightly upward; if true outcome shows volatility, add 0.5–1.0% downward adjustment to avoid false stability bias.
